parse_notes: Closed local observations on frozen synthetic benches. No generated answer, prompt, answer key, weight or machine log is published; no role is adopted.

LFM3-1.7B (Liquid AI), GGUF Q4_K_M (the publisher's own conversion), on the NVLink pair with -ts 6,18: all 24 layers (and the output layer) on GPU, 16,384-token context, one llama.cpp slot, so the eight requests of the house protocol are served one after another. llama.cpp's log also shows a CPU-mapped buffer of 205 MiB, against a file of 1,049 MiB; these records set ram_spill from 1,024 MiB, so it stays false here.

Same weights and image as lfm3-1.7b-one-card, the conditional arm on the other topology. Single stream 279.0 tok/s against 284.0 for lfm3-1.7b-one-card, aggregate 279.3 against 283.9 (three passes each, one slot): about 1.8 % slower single stream than one card, in all three passes.

One fixed order, one sequence: the pair ran last, with card 0 at 59-62 C and 1695 MHz at the start of its single-stream passes, against 41-50 C and 1935-1965 MHz on one card; the difference is an observation of this sequence, not an isolated topology effect.
The predeclared fit search had one setting, which loaded (6.3 s) and answered the canary.
Engine llama.cpp b11960. The published runs of other models used earlier or unversioned llama.cpp builds, or other engines, so their figures are not strictly comparable with these.
Single-stream energy rests on short windows: 722, 726, 771 J over the three passes (0.709, 0.705, 0.664 tok/J); in pass 3 the counter's mean power (418.6 W) exceeds the one-second peak (414.0 W).

Picked from a public model watch, downloaded at a fixed revision and checked by SHA-256, with its arms written and its fit searched before they ran; the conditional arm on the other topology ran after this model's planned arms had finished.
Run from 12:06 UTC to 13:32 UTC on 5 November, in a day window opened with the owner's go-ahead after the model watch, on the host's first pair. At each arm's start no process ran on the other pair.
